derivation: a primitive root; properly, to incline (the shoulder to a burden); but used only as denominative from H7926 (שְׁכֶם);
def: literally, to load up (on the back of man or beast), i.e. to start early in the morning
kjv: (arise, be up, get (oneself) up, rise up) early (betimes), morning.

occurrences.text: And he said, Behold now, my lords, turn in, I pray you, into your servant’s house, and tarry all night, and wash your feet, and ye shall rise up early, and go on your ways. And they said, Nay; but we will abide in the street all night.
words: and ye shall rise up early

occurrences.text: And Abraham gat up early in the morning to the place where he stood before the Lord:

words: that were with him rose up early

words: with thee and as soon as ye be up early
